style: a plain, friendly voice walking a colleague through a product demo; natural pace, conversational, not dramatic

scenes.text: Mei lives abroad. After a typhoon in Hualien, she gives fifty dollars to a small relief fund, on one condition: only for kids who lost their homes. Kindtrail checks that condition against every receipt, and shows her what her money bought.

Whoever starts a fund writes the condition as a sentence. Gemini turns it into rules: where the money can be spent, on what, for whom, and until when. Any rule can be changed. Adding medical care re-scores the sample pharmacy receipt right away. Once the fund is saved, every gift to it follows these rules.

Donors give through PayPal Checkout, in the sandbox. The server creates the order with the fund's code in custom ID, so the tag is stored on PayPal's side too. Here's a test buyer's gift that went all the way through: captured, and confirmed by a verified webhook.

In Hualien, a partner kitchen buys tarps, rice and kids' raincoats, and sends a photo of the receipt. Gemini reads each line, its price and where it is on the photo, in a couple of seconds. Then the rule engine decides, line by line. The prepaid gift card counts as cash, so donors' money can't pay for it.
At the charity, Lin sees every verdict with its reason, and which gifts will pay for it, oldest first. Approve sends the money to the kitchen with PayPal Payouts.
PayPal's webhook confirms the payout. Its signature is checked before the request is marked paid.

Mei gave her fifty dollars in October. Her receipt shows it paid for the four tarps and eighteen dollars of the rice, who shared the rest, the gift card it didn't touch, who approved it, and the PayPal transaction for the payout.
Kindtrail runs on PayPal Orders, the JavaScript SDK, Payouts, Webhooks and Transaction Search, with Gemini reading the receipts. You can try it at kindtrail dot onrender dot com.
